title: Sustained synchronization within posterior cortex during conscious perception

statements.text: IIT predicted sustained short-range, content-specific synchronization within posterior cortex, between early visual areas and category-selective areas, for the duration of a conscious percept.
statements.falsification_criteria: Preregistered: IIT is challenged if sustained content-specific synchronization between face and object selective areas and V1/V2 is absent.

prediction.resolution_criterion: The Cogitate study finds sustained content-specific synchronization between category-selective areas and V1/V2 for the stimulus duration, as specified in its preregistration.

standing.reason: The preregistered test found no sustained synchronization within posterior cortex, a stated failure condition for IIT.

sources.quote: IIT predicts sustained short-range connectivity within the posterior cortex, linking low-level sensory (V1/V2) with high-level category-selective areas (for example, fusiform face area and lateral occipital cortex)

Together, we devised and preregistered two experiments that test contrasting predictions of these theories concerning the location and timing of correlates of visual consciousness, which have been endorsed by the theories' proponents.
